description: A forward operating base commander must publish the next week's potable-water maintenance and distribution board, setting a tank-release time, a pump-maintenance window, a clinic reserve level, and the coordination controls needed to keep the plan executable.

shared_context.S1: The base operates three potable-water storage points: the South Tank, the North Tank, and the Clinic Tank.
shared_context.S2: Col. Mercer approves the weekly potable-water board and its supporting coordination actions.
shared_context.S3: The routine board releases treated water from the South Tank at 1200 on Wednesday, schedules North Tank pump maintenance on Thursday from 0900 to 1100, and maintains a 3,000-gallon Clinic Tank reserve.
shared_context.S4: The utilities section can provide a backup pump during a scheduled North Tank maintenance window, and the logistics section records changes to the water distribution board.
shared_context.S5: At the weekly water-systems review, Col. Mercer asks the logistics, utilities, and medical representatives to report any confirmed updates before approving the board.

PF1.text: Maj. Alvarez received the certified water-laboratory result this morning showing that the latest South Tank treatment batch requires exactly 6 hours of chlorine contact time before release, so that batch cannot be issued until 1800 Wednesday; the result is still attached to the logistics email and has not been entered on the distribution board.

PF2.text: SFC Okafor found during today's pump inspection that the North Tank pump needs its scheduled service moved to exactly Friday 1300-1500 because the replacement seal arrives Friday morning; the maintenance work order has not yet been updated.

PF3.text: Capt. Shah confirmed with the clinic this morning that Friday's immunization event requires the Clinic Tank reserve to be exactly 4,200 gallons from 0800 through 1200, rather than the routine 3,000 gallons; the medical support annex has not yet been cross-referenced with the water board.

acceptance_conditions: The South Tank treatment batch must not be released before 1800 Wednesday, with the certified laboratory result used as justification.
The North Tank pump maintenance must be scheduled for Friday 1300-1500, allowing either a hyphenated or word-separated time range.
The Clinic Tank reserve must be set to exactly 4,200 gallons for the immunization event.
The chlorine-contact requirement must be reflected either by the 1800 Wednesday release decision or by a corresponding commitment.
The replacement-seal timing must be reflected either by the Friday 1300-1500 maintenance decision or by a corresponding commitment.
The clinic reserve requirement must be reflected either by the 4,200-gallon decision or by a corresponding commitment.

decisive_facts.why: The 6-hour treatment requirement changes the South Tank release from 1200 to exactly 1800 Wednesday and supplies the fact that must be cited for the release decision.
The Friday replacement-seal arrival changes North Tank pump maintenance from Thursday 0900-1100 to exactly Friday 1300-1500.
The Friday immunization event changes the Clinic Tank reserve from 3,000 to exactly 4,200 gallons from 0800 through 1200.
